questions.q: Which operator does T-SQL use to concatenate strings?
questions.explain: T-SQL uses + for string concatenation, e.g. FirstName + ' ' + LastName.

questions.q: What happens if you concatenate a NULL value using +?
options: The entire concatenated result becomes NULL
The NULL is treated as an empty string automatically
The NULL is skipped and the rest concatenates normally
questions.explain: With +, a single NULL anywhere in the chain makes the whole expression evaluate to NULL.

questions.q: Which function concatenates strings while treating NULL as an empty string?
questions.explain: CONCAT() silently treats NULL arguments as empty strings, avoiding the all-or-nothing NULL problem that + has.

questions.q: In 'Customer: ' + FirstName + ' ' + LastName, what role does 'Customer: ' play?
options: A literal string woven into the concatenation alongside column values
questions.explain: Literal text in quotes can be mixed freely with column values in a concatenation expression.

questions.q: Why alias a concatenated expression like FirstName + ' ' + LastName?
options: Without an alias, the result column has an unreadable, unnamed header, same as any other expression
Aliasing is required syntactically for concatenation to work
It changes how NULL is handled
It converts the result to uppercase
questions.explain: Same rule as Lesson 5: any expression, including a concatenation, benefits from an explicit alias.
